songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Dark Star, tight acoustic sets and stellar New Riders interludes
ai_show_review.blurb: The May 15 1970 Fillmore East show delivers a soaring Dark Star and crisp acoustic numbers, with standout performances of Good Lovin' and Candyman. Jerry’s guitar tone shines, Phil provides thunderous bass, and Bill’s extended drum solo is a highlight. The recommended soundboard capture offers crystal‑clear audio throughout.
ai_show_review.review: May 15, 1970 at the Fillmore East remains one of the band’s most celebrated marathon dates, weaving together folk‑rock intimacy with psychedelic firepower. The evening opens with an acoustic set that flows seamlessly into New Riders of the Purple Sage interludes before launching into electric fireworks: a luminous Dark Star, a driving Good Lovin', and a ferocious turn on The Other One (as noted by reviewers even though it isn’t listed in the official setlist). Jerry Garcia’s guitar is described as immaculate—crisp, powerful, and soaring—while his pedal‑steel work adds an unexpected sparkle. Phil Lesh lays down a rolling thunder of bass that anchors the jams, especially on Cumberland Blues and Dark Star, and Bill Kreutzmann delivers an extended drum solo that reviewers call “great” and “crispy,” with Mickey Hart holding down a solid groove. Pigpen’s organ and vocals cut through the mix with surprising clarity, and Bob Weir’s rhythm work and humorous banter keep the energy buoyant throughout both acoustic and electric halves. The recommended soundboard recording captures all of this with bright mids, tight lows, and only minor tape glitches, making it an essential listen for anyone wanting to experience the full arc of this historic night.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: All three recordings are marked positive, repeatedly praising the soaring Dark Star, crisp guitar tone, powerful bass, extended drum solo and overall tight performance. Consistent language like “legendary,” “soaring,” “crisp,” and “stellar” across multiple sources justifies a strong positive adjustment.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture with excellent fidelity, minimal glitches, and the most complete representation of both acoustic and electric sets.

key_highlights: Soaring Dark Star with immaculate guitar tone
Tight acoustic sets and New Riders interludes add folk flavor
Extended drum solo by Bill Kreutzmann in the first electric set
Pigpen’s organ and vocal presence are clear and well‑balanced

band_performance.Jerry: Immaculate guitar tone, soaring solos and even pedal‑steel work make his playing the driving force of the night.
band_performance.Phil: Thunderous, rolling bass lines anchor the jams, especially on Cumberland Blues and Dark Star.
band_performance.Bob: Humorous banter adds charm; rhythm work is solid and vocals shine on Good Lovin' and other cuts.
band_performance.Mickey: Provides a steady groove that underpins Bill’s extended drum solo and the overall flow of the set.
band_performance.Billy: Delivers an extended, crisp drum solo praised as “great” and keeps the energy high throughout.
